# Anaconda channel catalog: main vs main-x

**This is not a source of truth.** It is a dated, regenerable citation of Anaconda's own sources — every figure carries the Anaconda URL it came from and the moment it was true. The sources of truth are anaconda.org and repo.anaconda.com; when in doubt, they're authoritative.

**Figures as of 2026-08-25** — `main` 5,469 packages · `main-x` 14,236 packages · 1,161 on both.

- main downloads (`api.anaconda.org/package/anaconda/<name>`): 98.6% coverage (5,392 of 5,469).
- main-x summaries (anaconda.org repocore): 99.2% coverage; a PyPI description fallback (exception-only) filled 6 more; 104 remain empty.
- main-x downloads: anaconda.org reports `download_count` = 0 for every main-x package (telemetry not populated for this channel yet; not zero usage — see the Summary sheet).
<!-- catalog:end -->

## Growth log

One row per refresh. These counts can't be reconstructed after the fact — `channeldata.json` only ever
describes now — so a week that isn't recorded is a week lost.

**On both** is an overlap, not a sum: package names that exist in `main` *and* `main-x`. **Distinct** counts
each name once across both channels (`main` + `main-x` − on both), which is the figure to quote for "how many
packages does Anaconda publish here". The two channels are not alternate copies of each other — `main-x`
supplements `main` and depends on it, and a shared name often carries a different latest version in each
channel, in both directions. The `on main-x?` / `on main?` columns in the workbook flag the overlap per row.

## What's in here

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `anaconda_channel_catalog.ipynb` | Notebook that (re)builds the catalog: integrity-checked fetches, refuses on truncation/partial data |
| `anaconda_channel_catalog.xlsx` | `main` · `main-x` · `Summary` (figures with source+date). Header line on top of each sheet (count, generation date, browse URL); autofilter on; sorted by downloads desc. |
| `download_counts_cache.json` | anaconda.org `ndownloads` cache for main (resume-safe) |
| `channel_history.csv` | Append-only package counts per refresh date; the growth log above is rendered from it |

Sources (all Anaconda-published):
- main contents/summaries: `repo.anaconda.com/pkgs/main/channeldata.json`; downloads: `api.anaconda.org/package/anaconda/<name>`.
- main-x contents/versions/licenses: `repo.anaconda.cloud/repo/main-x/` (Bearer token); summaries + download counts: anaconda.org repocore API (the .org front-end's own public API), with a PyPI description fallback used only where anaconda.org publishes nothing (counted+dated on Summary).

Refresh: `ANACONDA_REPO_TOKEN=<token> jupyter nbconvert --execute anaconda_channel_catalog.ipynb` (needs pandas, openpyxl). Re-running automatically picks up real main-x download counts once .org populates them, and rewrites the figures block above.

`.github/workflows/refresh-catalog.yml` does the same thing every Monday (and on demand from the Actions tab), committing the regenerated files. It needs `ANACONDA_REPO_TOKEN` as a repository secret; without it the main-x fetch fails and nothing is committed.
